newsitem.title: LEBANON: ING Barings sees Solidere shares rising.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings sees Solidere shares rising.

text.p: Shares in Solidere, Lebanon's biggest company, are trading at a large discount and can be expected to rise, according to a research document by ING Baring Securities Ltd.
It suggested that the value of the shares was $162-$172. Solidere's A and B shares currently trade on the Beirut Stock Exchange in a $112-$117 range.
The report was prepared in advance of Solidere's issue of Global Depositary Receipts earlier this week. ING Barings was a co-lead manager for the issue.
It said an ING Barings "residual value model" valued Solidere shares at $191 each, but this should be discounted 10-15 percent to $162-$172 due to regional and political risks.
Solidere, which is rebuilding central Beirut, was financially healthy and had no debt, although it expected to accumulate debt in the short term, the study said.
"We forecast earnings growth of 81.3 percent in 1996, 34.5 percent in 1997 and 28.2 percent in 1998," it said.
It estimated the 1996 price to earnings ratio at 55.8-59.3 and forecast that this would fall to 32.4-34.4 in 1998.
The relatively high ratios "can be justified given the fact that Solidere's revenues are expected to continue to show strong growth and probably peak between the years 2000 to 20005," the study said.

Much of the selling pressure on the shares stemmed from holders of A shares -- which are distributed to owners of property rights in the area Solidere is developing -- selling them as soon as they received them in exchange for their rights.
"With 75 percent of these shares now distributed, there should be much less local pressure on the share price," the study said.

"With much greater development now taking place and a number of recuperated buildings either completed or near completion, it is increasingly probable that local investor confidence in the share price will rise," it added.

"Fundamentally, the continuing improvement in international investor interest in the (Beirut) stock market, as witnessed by the success of a number of capital market issues, and the continuing capital flows into the country in general...will act as a trigger of buying interest from local investors, amongst others," the report said.
"The project to cross-list the Lebanese, Egyptian and Kuwait stock exchanges should add to regional interest, with the likelihood of solid Kuwait support for Lebanese shares," it said.
